words.basis_legend: The bold percentile is the one the player's profile uses for that metric.
words.stand_out_note: The six metrics where the player is furthest from the league average for the position, high or low. Lower-is-better metrics are counted from their better end; metrics with a hollow bar have no better end. Close variants of a metric already listed are left out.

words.gems_like_note: The players whose profiles are most like this one, in the same position, from other teams (provisional).
words.compare_top_note: The six metrics with the largest gap between the two players' league percentiles. Long pass completion, signature traits and metrics associated with team possession are left out, so team differences are not shown as player differences.
words.compare_same_group: Only players in the same position group can be compared.
words.signature_note: A holder / non-holder flag, not a percentile: most players in the group record none, so a rank would mostly compare zeros.

sections.title: Data
paragraphs: Event data from StatsBomb Open Data for the 2015/16 season: La Liga, the Premier League, Serie A and Ligue 1 in full, and part of the 1. Bundesliga. The 1. Bundesliga is not fully covered, so its players have no percentiles or profiles.
A player who moved clubs during the season has one row per club. Careers are never merged.

sections.title: Per 90 and minimum minutes
paragraphs: Counts are shown per 90 minutes played, next to the season total. Only players with at least 900 minutes are ranked, so a short run of games cannot make a player look elite. A rate such as pass completion is ranked only for players with enough attempts.

sections.title: Position groups
paragraphs: Each player is placed in one of six position groups by where they played most: goalkeepers, centre-backs, full-backs and wing-backs, central and defensive midfielders, attacking midfielders and wingers, and strikers. Players are only ever compared with their own group. Goalkeepers have no profile.

sections.title: Percentiles and bands
paragraphs: A percentile ranks a player within their own league and position group: 90 means they are ahead of about 90% of that group. Tables show it as a band (Top 1%, Top 5%, …, Bottom 5%); the exact number and the rank across all four full leagues are one tap away. Leagues are not adjusted for strength.
For a lower-is-better metric, such as times dispossessed, the percentile is counted from the better end, so a high number is always good.

sections.title: Hollow bars
paragraphs: Some metrics have no good or poor end. Style metrics describe how a player plays, not how well. Other metrics rise or fall with how much the team has the ball, so a high value may say more about the team than the player. Both show a hollow bar and read "higher than most", "around average" or "lower than most".

sections.title: Profile shape and family scores
paragraphs: The metrics are grouped into families such as Progressive passing or Aerial. A family score is the average of the player's league percentiles for the family's scored metrics; style metrics are not scored. Tap a family name to see what it measures: most families count how often a player does something, not how well.

A family is withheld for a position when its metrics are not shown to describe the player rather than the team. Defending is withheld for every position in this season, and Passing for all but strikers. There is no overall rating.

sections.title: Similar players
paragraphs: Similar players are found by comparing league percentiles on the profile's metrics within the same position group, with each family weighted equally. The closest players are listed; a player from the same team is marked. The method is provisional and will change.

sections.title: Defensive rate
paragraphs: In compare mode, tackles, interceptions, ball recoveries, pressures, blocks and clearances also show a rate per 100 opponent open-play passes while the player was on the pitch. The rate shows how often the player acts relative to how much the opponent had the ball; it does not remove team effects.

sections.title: Limits
paragraphs: One season only. No ages, because the open data has no birth dates. Team effects are not removed. Percentiles from different leagues rank players within their own league and are not adjusted for league strength.
